findings.description: The bucket has no ACL set explicitly and is commented as public with no public access block, meaning it may be readable/writable by anyone, exposing potentially sensitive data (customer-master.xlsx is stored here).
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default.
The bucket does not enable versioning, so objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, increasing risk from accidental or malicious data loss.
The bucket does not have access logging enabled, removing an important audit trail for access to potentially sensitive data.
A customer master data file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket which is public and unencrypted, exposing potentially sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket storing financial data, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket does not enable versioning, risking irreversible loss or tampering of financial data.
No logging configuration is present for this bucket, removing audit visibility into access of financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so operations data is stored unencrypted at rest.
The bucket does not configure a logging block, so there is no audit trail of access to this bucket.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving data science datasets unencrypted at rest.
